corePractice.en:
Self-Criticism Journal (5 minutes)
1. Prepare paper and a pen
2. Write down the negative things you said to yourself today
Examples: 'I messed up again,' 'I am stupid,' 'Why can I not even do this?'
3. Read each sentence and notice how it feels
4. Imagine, 'What if a friend said this?'

corePractice.en:
Self-Criticism Pattern Analysis (10 minutes)
1. Open the list you wrote yesterday
2. Look for repeated words or themes
Examples: 'stupid' 3 times, 'failure' 2 times, 'cannot do it' 4 times
3. Circle those words
4. Give the pattern a name
Examples: 'perfectionist criticism,' 'doubting my ability,' 'comparing myself to others'

1. 어제 적은 목록을 펼칩니다
2. 반복되는 단어나 주제를 찾습니다
예: '멍청하다' 3번, '실패' 2번, '못한다' 4번
3. 이 단어들을 동그라미로 표시합니다
4. 패턴에 이름을 붙입니다
예: '완벽주의 비판', '능력 의심', '타인 비교'

Find just one pattern. Whether it is 'doubting my ability' or 'comparing myself to others,' one is enough.

If you discovered one repeated pattern -> success!

title.en: Practice Speaking as You Would to a Friend

morningRitual.en: Today, I will speak to myself like a friend.
morningRitual.ko: 나는 오늘 나에게 친구처럼 말할 것입니다.

corePractice.en:
Self-Talk Reframe (real time, all day)
1. When you notice self-criticism, pause for a moment
2. Take 3 deep breaths
3. Think about what you would say to a friend in the same situation
4. Say that sentence out loud to yourself
Example:
 'I messed up again. I am stupid.' (self-criticism)
->  'What would I say to a friend?'
->  'Mistakes are part of learning. You can do better next time.' (self-compassion)
corePractice.ko:
자기대화 전환 (실시간 (하루 종일))
1. 자기비판이 감지되면 잠시 멈춥니다
2. 심호흡을 3번 합니다
3. 같은 상황을 친구에게 어떻게 말할지 생각합니다
4. 그 문장을 소리 내어 자신에게 말합니다
예시:
 '또 실수했어, 멍청해' (자기비판)
→  '친구라면 뭐라고 말할까?'
→  '실수는 배우는 과정이야. 다음엔 더 잘할 수 있어' (자기자비)

whyItWorks.en: It breaks the double standard of being compassionate to others while being harsh toward yourself.
whyItWorks.ko: 타인에게는 자비롭지만 자신에게는 가혹한 이중 잣대를 깨뜨립니다.

expectedResistance.en: It may feel awkward and not sincere.
expectedResistance.ko: 어색하고 진심처럼 느껴지지 않을 수 있습니다.

breakthroughStrategy.en:
It is okay if it does not feel sincere. Try it mechanically, like an actor rehearsing lines. The brain learns through repetition.
 Evening reflection

How kind was I to myself today? (0-10)
 Today's small win
If you tried speaking to yourself like a friend even once -> success!
breakthroughStrategy.ko:
진심이 아니어도 괜찮습니다. 배우가 대사를 연습하듯 기계적으로 해보세요. 뇌는 반복으로 배웁니다.
 저녁 성찰

오늘 나는 나에게 얼마나 친절했나요? (0-10점)
 오늘의 작은 승리
친구처럼 말하기를 1번이라도 시도했다면 → 성공!

morningRitual.en: I will create my own self-compassion phrases.
morningRitual.ko: 나만의 자기자비 문구를 만들 것입니다.

corePractice.en:
Write Personalized Self-Compassion Phrases (15 minutes)
1. Write these questions on paper:
• What words do I want to hear when things are hardest?
• What would I say to a close friend in the same situation?
• What would someone who cares about me say?
2. Use your answers to create 3 phrases:
Template:
A) 'This is a difficult moment. (acknowledge the situation)'
B) 'Many people experience this kind of difficulty. (common humanity)'
C) 'I can be kind to myself. (self-kindness)'
Example, tailored to a perfectionist pattern:
A) 'It is okay not to be perfect.'
B) 'Mistakes are part of being human.'
C) 'I am doing well enough.'
3. Save them in your smartphone notes app
corePractice.ko:
개인 맞춤 자기자비 문구 작성 (15분)
1. 종이에 이 질문들을 씁니다:
• 가장 힘들 때 듣고 싶은 말은?
• 친한 친구가 같은 상황이라면 뭐라고 할까?
• 나를 아끼는 사람이라면 뭐라고 말할까?
2. 답을 바탕으로 3개 문구를 만듭니다:
템플릿:
A) '이것은 힘든 순간이다. (상황 인정)'
B) '많은 사람들이 이런 어려움을 겪는다. (보편성)'
C) '나는 나에게 친절할 수 있다. (자기친절)'
예시 (완벽주의 패턴 맞춤):
A) '완벽하지 않아도 괜찮다.'
B) '실수는 인간의 일부다.'
C) '나는 충분히 잘하고 있다.'
3. 스마트폰

morningRitual.ko: 일어나자마자 자기자비 문구를 3번 읽습니다.

corePractice.en:
Morning Self-Compassion Routine (3 minutes)
1. Turn off your alarm and sit up in bed
2. Open the phrases you created yesterday on your smartphone
3. Read each phrase slowly 3 times
(9 total repetitions: 3 phrases x 3 times)
4. Place your hand on your chest as you read the final phrase
5. Say, 'I am enough for this day, too'

corePractice.en:
80% vs. 100% Comparison Experiment (10 minutes theory + real-time application)
1. Divide a sheet of paper in two (left: 100% / right: 80%)
2. On the left side (100%), write:
• How long would it take to do this perfectly?
• Stress level? (0-10)
• Does it make me delay starting?
• Result: will it be completed?
3. On the right side (80%), write:
• How long would it take to do only 80%?
• Stress level? (0-10)
• Is it easier to start?
• Result: likelihood of completion?
4. Choose one small task for today
Examples: writing an email, cleaning, cooking
5. Intentionally do only 80% and stop
• Email: skip spell-check
• Cleaning: only the visible areas

• Cooking: a simple version

2. 왼쪽(100%)에 적기:
• 완벽하게 하려면 시간이 얼마나 걸리나?
• 스트레스 수준은? (0-10)
• 시작을 미루게 되나?
• 결과: 완성 여부?
3. 오른쪽(80%)에 적기:
• 80%만 하려면 시간이 얼마나 걸리나?
• 스트레스 수준은? (0-10)
• 시작이 쉬운가?
• 결과: 완성 가능성?
4. 오늘 할 작은 작업 1개를 선택합니다
예: 이메일 쓰기, 청소, 요리
5. 의도적으로 80%만 하고 멈춥니다
• 이메일: 맞춤법 검사 생략
• 청소: 눈에 보이는 곳만

• 요리: 간단한 버전

Pomodoro 80% Technique (25 minutes x 2 rounds)
1. Choose a task for today
2. Set a timer for 25 minutes
3. Before you start, say this:
'My goal is to complete only 80% within 25 minutes'
4. Start working -> stop no matter what after 25 minutes
(Even if it is 60% complete, OK. Even if it is 90%, stop)
5. Take a 5-minute break

• Only lightly refine the result from round 1 (not perfectly)
• After 25 minutes, submit/mark it complete no matter what
7. Rate the completeness yourself (0-100%)
8. Say, 'This is enough'

corePractice.en:

1. Choose a current work in progress
(about 50-70% complete)
2. Choose one person you trust
(coworker, friend, mentor)
3. Say this:
'This is a draft and it is not finished yet.

[Specific question: for example, is the structure clear?]'
4. Receive feedback

• Feedback received:
• Did the criticism you expected happen?
• What reaction actually happened?

• 받은 피드백:
• 예상했던 비판이 나왔나요?
• 실제로 나온 반응은?
• 불완전함을 공유한 후 느낌은?

corePractice.en:
Explore the Roots of Perfectionism (20 minutes)

• Who do I want to look perfect for?
• What will happen if I am not perfect?

• What has perfectionism taken away from me?

title.en: You Are Not the Only One Struggling

morningRitual.en: Everyone is fighting their own battle.
morningRitual.ko: 모두가 자기만의 전쟁을 치르고 있습니다.

corePractice.en:
Common Humanity Journal (10 minutes)
1. Recall a difficult moment from today or recently
2. Answer these questions:
• Is there anyone else who has been through a similar situation?
• Who in the world might be feeling the same pain right now?
• Is this pain something any human being could experience?
3. Complete this sentence:
'I am not the only one. [Specific situation]
is a universal human pain that many people experience.'
4. Send this thought to someone who may be going through the same pain:
'You must be having a hard time too. Let us endure this together.'
corePractice.ko:
공통 인간성 일기 (10분)
1. 오늘 또는 최근에 겪은 힘든 순간을 떠올립니다
2. 이 질문에 답해봅니다:
• 나와 비슷한 상황을 겪은 사람이 또 있을까?
• 전 세계에서 지금 이 순간 나와 같은 고통을 느끼는 사람은?
• 이 고통은 인간이라면 누구나 경험할 수 있는 것일까?
3. 이 문장을 완성합니다:
'나만 이런 게 아니구나. [구체적 상황]은/는
많은 사람들이 경험하는 인간의 보편적 고통이다.'
4. 같은 고통을 겪고 있을 누군가에게 보내는 마음:
'당신도 힘들겠네요. 우리 함께 버텨요.'

whyItWorks.en: Isolation amplifies pain. When you move from 'only me' to 'us,' the pain decreases.
whyItWorks.ko: 고립감은 고통을 증폭시킵니다. '나만'에서 '우리'로 전환하면 고통이 줄어듭니다.

expectedResistance.en: You may think, 'But other people handle it better than I do.'
expectedResistance.ko: '하지만 다른 사람들은 나보다 잘 해내잖아' 같은 생각이 들 수 있습니다.

breakthroughStrategy.en:
What appears on the outside is different from reality. Everyone posts only the good parts on social media. Remember the invisible battles.
 Evening reflection
Did your perspective shift even slightly today from 'only me' to 'us'?
 Today's small win
If you empathized with someone else's pain and felt connection -> success!

기억하세요.

오늘 '나만'에서 '우리'로 시각이 조금이라도 바뀌었나요?
 오늘의 작은 승리
타인의 고통에 공감하고 연결감을 느꼈다면 → 성공!

title.en: Collect Evidence That 'I Am Not the Only Weird One'

morningRitual.en: Imperfection is part of being human.
morningRitual.ko: 불완전함은 인간의 조건입니다.

corePractice.en:
Collect Evidence of Universality (15 minutes)
1. Write 3 things you have thought, 'Am I the only one like this?' about:
Examples: mistakes, failure, anxiety, self-doubt, loneliness
2. Find evidence for each item (online search OK):
• Statistics: 'percentage of people who experience OO'
• Other people's stories: forums, blogs, books
• Experiences of people around you (ask them)
3. Summarize each item like this:
[My thought] I thought I was the only one:
-> [Evidence] In reality:
Example:
[My thought] I think I am the only one who procrastinates
-> [Evidence] 75% of college students experience habitual procrastination (Steel, 2007)
4. How do you feel now that you know this?
corePractice.ko:
보편성 증거 수집 (15분)
1. 내가 '나만 이런가?'라고 생각했던 것 3가지 적기:
예: 실수, 실패, 불안, 자기의심, 외로움
2. 각 항목에 대해 증거 찾기 (온라인 검색 OK):
• 통계 자료: 'OO 겪는 사람 비율'
• 다른 사람들의 이야기: 포럼, 블로그, 책
• 주변 사람들의 경험 (물어보기)

corePractice.en:
Practice 'Us' Language (15 minutes)
1. Write self-critical thoughts in 'only me' language:
Examples: 'I guess I am the only one who cannot do this'
'Why am I so anxious?'
'I feel like I am the only lonely one'
2. Change the same content into 'us' language:
Examples: 'Many people experience this kind of difficulty'
'Anxiety is a universal human emotion'
'Loneliness is something everyone experiences'
3. Add concrete evidence:
Examples: '70% of workers experience impostor syndrome (Sakulku, 2011)'
'Lifetime prevalence of anxiety disorders is 30% (Kessler et al., 2005)'
'Loneliness epidemiology research: 40% of adults experience it (Cigna, 2020)'
4. Read these 'us' sentences out loud (3 times)
5. Throughout today, whenever self-criticism arises:
Consciously change 'only me' -> 'us' in your language

1. 자기비판적 생각을 '나만' 언어로 적기:

2. 같은 내용을 '우리' 언어로 바꾸기:
예: '많은 사람들이 이런 어려움을 겪어'

4. 이 '우리' 문장들을 크게 읽어봅니다 (3회)

Loving-Kindness Meditation (15 minutes)
1. Sit comfortably and close your eyes
2. First, to yourself (2 minutes):

'May I be free from suffering'
'May I be peaceful'
3. To someone you love (3 minutes):
Picture [name]'s face:
'May you be happy'
'May you be free from suffering'
'May you be peaceful'

(someone you passed by today)
Repeat the same phrases
5. To a difficult person (3 minutes):
(someone who has made things hard for you)
Repeat the same phrases, as much as you can

'May all beings be free from suffering'
'May all beings be peaceful'

corePractice.en:
Consciously Let Go of 'Pretending to Be Perfect' (all day, 10 minutes to prepare)
1. Write a 'pretending to be perfect' list:
Areas where I usually pretend to be perfect:
□ Work (pretending not to make mistakes)
□ Relationships (pretending I am always fine)
□ Appearance (pretending I have no flaws)
□ Emotions (pretending to be positive)
□ Ability (pretending I know everything)
2. Today's experiment: intentionally show a 'small imperfection'
Level 1 (safe):
• Honestly say, 'I do not know this well'
• Ask for help
Level 2 (moderate):
• Admit, 'Actually, I made a mistake too'
• Say, 'I have been having a hard time lately'
Level 3 (challenge):
• Go out without makeup

• Post an imperfect moment on social media
3. Observe after each experiment:
• Expected: [What did you think would happen?]
• Actual: [What actually happened?]
• Feeling: [How did it feel?]
4. Summarize in the evening:
• What I lost when I let go of pretending to be perfect:
• What I gained when I let go of pretending to be perfect:

□ 능력 (다 아는 척)

• 완벽한 척을 내려놓았을 때 얻은 것:

corePractice.en:

2. Write 3-5 of your core values in the roots
Examples: growth, connection, honesty, creativity, contribution
Question: 'What truly matters to me?'
3. Write moments when these values supported you on the trunk
Example: 'growth' -> a time when you got back up after failure
4. Write what you want to do with these values on the branches
Example: 'connection' -> have a deep conversation with a friend once a month
5. Write the emotions you feel when you live these values on the fruit

예: 성장, 연결, 정직, 창의성, 기여
질문: '내가 정말 중요하게 여기는 것은?'

Did you practice one of your core values today? How did it feel?

corePractice.en:
Create a Self-Compassion Emergency Kit (25 minutes)
1. Write a 'hard day checklist':
□ The voice of self-criticism gets louder
□ Perfectionist pressure gets stronger
□ Everything feels like my fault
□ It feels like people dislike me
(Add 3-5 of your own signals)
2. Write 'self-compassion first aid' for each signal:
Example:
Signal: The voice of self-criticism gets louder
-> First aid:
• Place your hand on your chest and breathe deeply 3 times
• Say, 'This is really hard right now'
• Read your Day 4 self-compassion phrases 3 times
3. Write a 'help request list':
• 3 people you can call
• 2 places you can go

• Comforting content (books, videos, songs)
4. Write a 'small comfort list':
• Things you can do within 5 minutes (warm tea, walk, music)
• Things you can do within 10 minutes (shower, yoga, journal)
• Things you can do within 30 minutes (walk in nature, movie)
5. Organize all of this on one page in your notebook
6. Take a photo and save it so you can view it anytime

자기자비 비상 키트 만들기 (25분)
1. '힘든 날 체크리스트' 작성:
□ 자기비판 목소리가 커진다
□ 완벽주의 압박이 심해진다
□ 모든 게 내 잘못 같다
□ 사람들이 날 싫어할 것 같다
(나만의 신호 3-5개 추가)
2. 각 신호별 '자기자비 응급처치' 작성:
예시:
신호: 자기비판 목소리가 커진다
→ 응급처치:
• 손을 가슴에 얹고 3번 깊게 호흡
• '지금 정말 힘들구나' 말해주기
• Day 4 자기자비 문구 3번 읽기
3. '도움 요청 리스트' 작성:
• 전화할 수 있는 사람 3명
• 찾아갈 수 있는 공간 2곳

• 위로받은 콘텐츠 (책, 영상, 노래)
4. '작은 위안 목록' 작성:
• 5분 안에 할 수 있는 것 (따뜻한 차, 산책, 음악)
• 10분 안에 할 수 있는 것 (샤워, 요가, 일기)
• 30분 안에 할 수 있는 것 (자연 속 걷기, 영화)
5. 이 모든 것을 노트 한 페이지에 정리합니다
6. 사진을 찍어 언제든 볼 수 있게 저장합니다

corePractice.en:
Design a Self-Compassion Routine (20 minutes)
1. Look back on the past 25 days:
• Which 3 practices helped the most?
• What do I want to continue?
• What felt burdensome?
2. Design your own 'daily routine' (3 steps):
 Morning routine (5 minutes):
Example: Read Day 5 self-compassion phrases + place your hand on your chest
 Daytime routine (as needed):
Example: Whenever you notice self-criticism, say 'This is hard right now'
 Evening routine (10 minutes):
Example: Day 6 evening check-in (one small win from today)
3. Write a 'maintenance strategy':
• Set calendar reminders
• Create a routine tracker (checklist)
• Choose one 'self-compassion check-in day' each month

4. Prepare for obstacles:
• Busy day: minimum routine (1-minute version)
• When you miss a day: choose 'start again' instead of self-criticism
5. Write this routine on paper and place it somewhere visible

자기자비 루틴 디자인 (20분)
1. 지난 25일을 돌아봅니다:
• 가장 도움이 된 실천 3가지는?

title.en: Write a Letter to Your Future Self

morningRitual.en: Six months from now, I will be a more compassionate person.

corePractice.en:
Write a Future Letter (30 minutes)
1. Set the recipient: 'To myself 6 months from now'
2. Letter content (4-part structure):
 Part 1: Me right now
• What were you like before beginning the 28-day journey?
• What was hardest?
• What change did you want?
 Part 2: What I learned from the journey
• The 3 most important insights you discovered during the 28 days
• Which practice helped you the most?
• What was the hardest moment you still got through?
 Part 3: What I want my future self to remember
• What to remember 6 months from now when things get hard again
• One sentence you must never forget
• A habit you hope to keep practicing
 Part 4: Encouragement and promise
• A warm encouragement message to your future self

• End with a promise to 'check in again in 6 months'
3. Put the letter in an envelope and write 'Open in 6 months'
4. Set a calendar reminder for 6 months from now

미래 편지 작성 (30분)
1. 편지 수신인 설정: '6개월 후의 나에게'
2. 편지 내용 (4단계 구조):
 1부: 지금의 나
• 28일 여정을 시작하기 전 나는 어땠나요?
• 무엇이 가장 힘들었나요?
• 어떤 변화를 원했나요?
 2부: 여정에서 배운 것
• 28일 동안 발견한 가장 중요한 깨달음 3가지
• 나를 가장 많이 도운 실천은?
• 가장 힘들었지만 해냈던 순간은?
 3부: 미래에 당부하고 싶은 것
• 6개월 후, 다시 힘들어질 때 기억해야 할 것
• 절대 잊지 말아야 할 한 문장
• 계속 실천했으면 하는 습관
 4부: 응원과 약속
• 미래의 나에게 따뜻한 응원 메시지

• '6개월 후 재검사'를 약속하며 마무리
3. 편지를 봉투에 넣고 '6개월 후 열기'라고 적습니다
4. 캘린더에 6개월 후 알림을 설정합니다

whyItWorks.en: A conversation with your future self solidifies current growth and creates a long-term perspective.
whyItWorks.ko: 미래 자기와의 대화는 현재의 성장을 굳히고, 장기적 관점을 만듭니다.

expectedResistance.en: Doubt may arise: 'What is the point?' or 'I will forget everything in 6 months anyway.'
expectedResistance.ko: '이게 무슨 소용이야?', '6개월 후엔 다 까먹을 텐데' 같은 회의가 생길 수 있습니다.

breakthroughStrategy.en:
If you do not record this moment's insights now, you really will forget them. This letter is a gift for your future self.
 Evening reflection
What emotions came up while writing the letter? Pride? Sadness? Hope? All of them are precious.
 Today's small win
If you completed a letter to your future self -> success!

지금 이 순간의 깨달음을 기록하지 않으면, 정말로 까먹습니다. 이 편지는 미래의 나를 위한
선물입니다.

corePractice.en:
Write a Personalized Self-Compassion Manifesto (30 minutes)

• Reread your notes from the beginning
• Highlight sentences that stay with you
• Check the 5 practices that helped the most
2. Write 'my definition of self-compassion':
• What does self-compassion mean to me?
• Define it in one sentence
Example: 'Self-compassion means treating myself like a friend'
3. Write 5 'self-compassion principles' of your own:
Principles from Days 1-27 that you want to remember for life
Examples:
1. When I notice self-criticism, pause and breathe
2. Believe that I am enough even when I am not perfect
3. Ask for help when things are hard
4. Remember that my pain is a universal human experience

Example: 'In this moment, I am on my side'
5. Organize it as a 'manifesto':
• Write it beautifully on one A4 page (handwriting recommended)
• Top: my definition of self-compassion
• Middle: 5 principles
• Bottom: my personal mantra
• Add your signature and date
6. Take a photo, and keep the original somewhere visible

나만의 자기자비 선언문을 완성하고 서명했다면 → 성공!
